author: Codex
alignment_method: Acoustic word timestamps measured on the actual final tempo-adjusted audio, mapped to authored text. Corrections/interpolation around recognition differences are not claimed perfectly frame-exact.

scenes.text: Your first Pokemon battle ends with you carrying Charmander into a Pokemon Center.
scenes.action: Medium view by the Center doorway: Nico carries the exhausted little Charmander across both forearms, one tail held clear of his blue jacket, no injury or blood.

scenes.text: The trainer who beat you is already on his way to the next town.
scenes.action: Milo walks away along the rear path with Squirtle beside his boots, looking back briefly. Keep foreground court empty, no Nico or ghost of the earlier battle.

scenes.text: You're holding your partner's tail clear of your jacket, trying to remember whether its flame looked this small before the fight.
scenes.action: Close detail of Nico's WHITE supporting mittens and Charmander's continuous tail; its small flame is separate from the sleeve. Show part of the red awning behind them.

scenes.text: You wanted eight badges and a shot at the Kanto League. But right now, you'd settle for Charmander opening its eyes.
scenes.action: Closer face-and-partner shot: Nico lowers his gaze toward Charmander's shut eyes and grips it securely. No imagined Charizard, badge collage or inset.

scenes.text: That trip to the Champion starts here, with you waiting outside the treatment room.
scenes.action: Nico sits on the left blue bench facing the central treatment doorway, hands together, cap lowered slightly. Empty counter and waiting room, no patient duplicated.

scenes.text: The nurse takes Charmander from your arms and asks what happened.
scenes.action: At the right counter Nico carefully passes Charmander to the mint nurse over the cream mat; their hands support the same single animal, tail safe away from clothing.

scenes.text: You explain the battle against Squirtle, the water attack, and the command you gave after Charmander stumbled.
scenes.action: The earlier battle as one normal full-frame scene: Squirtle on the far side sends a small water stream at Charmander in front of Nico. Milo gives one command from behind Squirtle. No ghost overlay.

scenes.text: She asks why you didn't call it back. You have an answer ready about getting through the opponent's defenses. It sounds ridiculous while she checks your Pokemon.
scenes.action: Nurse checks Charmander seated tiredly on the cream mat; Nico on the patient side attempts an explanation with one hesitant palm-up white mitten. Same counter and unit positions.

scenes.text: She takes it through the doorway, and you sit down with an unused Potion in your pocket.
scenes.action: Nurse carries Charmander toward the central rear doorway; Nico lowers himself onto the left bench. Patient not simultaneously left on the mat.

scenes.text: You packed it that morning. You forgot it existed when someone challenged you.
scenes.action: Close shot of Nico looking at the unused small purple Potion bottle in his white hand, with the open jacket pocket visible. No lettering on bottle or phone UI.

scenes.text: Through the waiting-room window, you can see the road leaving Viridian City. Other trainers pass with partners walking beside them.
scenes.action: Nico looks toward the LEFT window from the bench. Outside only, Jonah and Trader pass along a simple pavement with Eevee and Poliwag beside them. No extra people, no exterior Center building copied inside the room.

scenes.text: Your map is spread across your knees, with Pewter City circled. You were supposed to get there before your rival, Milo.
scenes.action: Nico studies a cream route map across his knees on the left bench; a red circle and simple path mark Pewter without lettering. The mint counter and central doorway retain their positions.

scenes.text: Eventually, the nurse comes back. Charmander will recover. You get to bring it home with you, and she suggests learning when to stop a battle before starting another one.
scenes.action: Nurse returns from the central doorway carrying recovering Charmander; Nico rises from the bench and reaches to receive it. The same nurse cap, mint coat and pure-white head.

scenes.text: Charmander reaches for your sleeve when you pick it up. You stay until it can walk without leaning against your leg.
scenes.action: Charmander touches Nico's blue sleeve with one paw while he crouches beside it; it has recovered enough to stand on its own feet near his boot. No extra hands or patients.

scenes.text: Earlier that morning, choosing Charmander had felt easy. Professor Oak had shown you the starter Pokemon at his lab in Pallet Town.
scenes.action: Oak gestures to the three CLOSED starter balls on the right wooden desk. Nico and Milo face him from the patient/visitor side; empty chair beside Nico, window left. No Pokemon visible yet.

scenes.text: Squirtle had inspected Milo's shoe. Bulbasaur had settled beside the table.
scenes.action: Closer lower view beside the starter desk: Squirtle inspects Milo's brown boot, Bulbasaur rests beside a table leg. Do not add Nico, Oak or a second creature of either species.

scenes.text: Charmander had tried to climb onto your chair, missed, and looked at you as if you were responsible for moving it.
scenes.action: Charmander struggles to reach the wooden chair beside Nico, paws on the chair edge, hind feet still near the floor; Nico bends toward it. No floating chair or raised platform.

scenes.text: You held out a hand. It grabbed your fingers and hauled itself up.
scenes.action: Close handoff: Nico offers a simple white mitten and Charmander grabs its thumb area, using it to climb onto the same chair. One clear supporting contact, no human fingers drawn onto the creature.

scenes.text: You pictured that little orange Pokemon growing into a Charizard, and agreed to take care of it without having much idea what that involved.
scenes.action: Nico kneels beside the chair and agrees to care for Charmander, Oak observing beside the desk. Show their actual present choice, no future Charizard, thought bubble or double starter.

scenes.text: Oak gave you a Pokedex, and Milo challenged you almost as soon as you left.
scenes.action: Oak places one small red closed Pokedex into Nico's hands; Milo by the back-left door gestures toward the court outside. One device, no written interface.

scenes.text: You'd watched enough battles to know what the commands sounded like. Unfortunately, knowing when to shout an attack didn't make you good at choosing one.
scenes.action: First novice match: Nico gives an overconfident forward command; Charmander advances across the court while Squirtle remains farther away near Milo. No projectile or damage yet.

scenes.text: Squirtle stayed out of reach, and you kept sending Charmander forward.
scenes.action: Squirtle sidesteps backward while Charmander cannot close the gap; Nico points from his own trainer side. Keep four distinct subjects, no second Nico or camera inset.

scenes.text: Milo won, asked if you were all right, and left while you were still pretending the loss didn't bother you.
scenes.action: The match is over. Milo asks a concerned question, Squirtle at his feet; Nico holds a stiff posture with tired Charmander beside him. No victory text or referee.

scenes.text: Once Charmander tried to take another step, you finally noticed how tired it was. That's how your journey reached the Pokemon Center before it reached its first Gym.
scenes.action: Charmander stumbles while trying to walk; Nico bends to catch and carry it, concern replacing his stiff pose. No fainted duplicate on ground and carried version at once.

scenes.text: Your second attempt at leaving town is less impressive. Charmander walks beside you, and you stop when it stops.
scenes.action: Nico and Charmander walk along the woodland route; he stops as his small partner pauses beside the low right rock. Both physically grounded, calm eye-height medium shot.

scenes.text: You practice a recall with its Poke Ball before you attempt another battle. It takes you a while to get the timing right.
scenes.action: Nico practices recalling Charmander, aiming the active red-white ball from a white mitten toward the single partner. One thin red recall light, no miniature animal in the ball or second Charmander.

scenes.text: At a fork in the path, Charmander waits for a command and you realize you've been studying the map instead of watching where you're going.
scenes.action: At the central fork Nico looks down at his map while Charmander waits and looks toward him; post stays blank, same log and low rock. No invented written road signs.

scenes.text: You start making your plans before setting off. You also put the Potion somewhere you can reach without emptying every pocket.
scenes.action: Nico folds the map and puts the purple Potion into an accessible jacket pocket, Charmander waiting beside him. Medium view of action, not another static landscape.

scenes.text: By evening, you've discovered several things the televised battles leave out. Charmander wants food while you're still pitching the tent.
scenes.action: Late-afternoon campsite: Nico fastens the LEFT green tent entrance while Charmander points its snout toward the EMPTY orange bowl. No pitched tent duplication, keep log and firepit positions.

scenes.text: A Pokemon with a flame on its tail needs a sensible place to sleep, away from the fabric.
scenes.action: Nico arranges a small safe sleeping mat beside the tent entrance; Charmander's tail and flame remain outside and away from fabric. No tail inside tent or burning canvas.

scenes.text: Your shoes are rubbing, and the town you thought was nearby is farther away than it looked on the map.
scenes.action: Seated on the right log Nico loosens one brown boot and checks his route map on his knees; his other boot remains worn. Same campsite, no disconnected legs or extra shoes.

scenes.text: You spend part of the night checking whether your partner is comfortable.
scenes.action: Night variant of this same campsite: Nico kneels to check Charmander resting on its mat near the tent; keep face and hands flat pure white despite night light. No campfire against tail or tent.

scenes.text: In the morning, it wakes you by sitting on your chest. Apparently, you're getting better at the job, because it expects breakfast now.
scenes.action: Morning: Nico lies on his tan mat just outside the tent and Charmander sits lightly on his covered chest looking toward the food bowl. One Nico, two natural arms, no duplicated sleeping portrait.

scenes.text: On the way north, you try to catch a Pidgey. Your first throw lands beside it.
scenes.action: Nico's thrown active ball has landed beside a small Pidgey on the path. He has just finished the throw; Charmander stands next to him. One loose ball, no captured bird inside it.

scenes.text: Pidgey looks at the ball, looks at you, and flies into a branch you can't reach. Charmander follows it with its eyes while you retrieve the ball from the grass.
scenes.action: Pidgey perches on a high left branch, out of reach; Nico bends to pick the failed ball from the grass while Charmander looks up. Distinct new action, same fork and log.

scenes.text: Later, you find another Pidgey near a clearing and take the time to watch it.
scenes.action: At the clearing edge Nico and Charmander watch a calm Pidgey near the low rock before acting. This is one later bird, not a pair of Pidgey or the earlier attempt overlaid.

scenes.text: You give Charmander a short command, stop the battle before it goes too far, and make your throw while the bird is close.
scenes.action: Charmander stops advancing at Nico's raised white palm; the active ball arcs toward the nearby Pidgey. No explosive flames, two birds or spectator crowd.

scenes.text: When the ball settles, you check it instead of celebrating over it.
scenes.action: Nico crouches to check one closed capture ball settled on the ground; Charmander waits beside his boot. Pidgey is INSIDE the ball and must not also be visible on a branch.

scenes.text: Now you're responsible for a Pokemon that can leave through the top of your campsite. Pidgey needs room to fly, and Charmander dislikes being startled by something landing behind it.
scenes.action: Pidgey flies down from the right log toward camp, and Charmander turns at the unexpected arrival. Nico stays between tent and log, trying to coordinate both partners.

scenes.text: You spend a training session trying to get both of them comfortable around each other.
scenes.action: Nico gives each partner space during a calm exercise, with Charmander on the left mat and Pidgey landing on the right log. Bowls remain near the tent entrance until moved in the next shot.

scenes.text: Pidgey steals a piece of Charmander's food. Charmander snaps at it. You separate the bowls and wonder how anyone manages a larger team.
scenes.action: Nico separates the orange and blue bowls after Pidgey snatches a crumb and Charmander objects. Two bowls placed apart on the ground, one of each creature, no human-like creature hands.

scenes.text: By the time you reach Pewter City, you've started to understand your partners. Brock is about to show you how much work remains.
scenes.action: Nico enters the rear-left Gym doorway with Charmander, Brock waiting on the far-right trainer platform. Establish the rock court without Onix or additional challengers yet.

scenes.text: His Gym has a rock-covered battlefield and an Onix that makes Charmander look very small.
scenes.action: Wide but subject-readable match setup: single Onix curves along the far half of the rock court, towering over little Charmander on Nico's near side. No detached stone-snake segments or duplicate head.

scenes.text: You knew Brock used Rock-type Pokemon. You came anyway because you wanted to see whether enough determination would solve the matchup.
scenes.action: Nico gives Charmander a determined forward command as Brock and the same Onix wait across the court. Mid-height view, humans compact and round white, no body inflation from battle setting.

scenes.text: Charmander's fire leaves Onix ready to continue. You call another attack, see Charmander struggling to find space, and reach for its ball.
scenes.action: Charmander's modest fire attack has left Onix ready to advance. Nico reaches for the active ball while his tired starter searches for room between low rocks. One opponent, no huge firestorm.

scenes.text: You withdraw it while it can still stand. Brock wins.
scenes.action: Nico lowers the recall ball after withdrawing his partner; Brock acknowledges the result from his far trainer side. NO Charmander visible while it is in the closed ball.

scenes.text: You leave with an empty badge case, but this time your partner walks out beside you instead of being carried to the nurse.
scenes.action: Outside the immediate battlefield near the left entry, Nico opens the empty badge case while Charmander walks beside his boot. All eight small slots empty, no invented earned badges.

scenes.text: Brock suggests building a team that can handle more than one kind of opponent.
scenes.action: Brock talks to Nico beside the edge of the quiet court, gesturing toward Nico's empty case; no battle Pokemon or ghost starter added from the identity guides.

scenes.text: You find a Poliwag at a pond during your training outside town. Catching it takes patience, and getting it to work with you takes longer.
scenes.action: At the stony LEFT bank Nico patiently watches a single Poliwag in the shallow right water before a capture. Poliwag has a tail and NO arms; no Poliwhirl substituted.

scenes.text: It knows how to move in water. Your directions on dry ground confuse it.
scenes.action: Poliwag has emerged from the pond and pauses awkwardly on the dry bank; Nico gives a short pointing gesture. Show its tiny feet, tail and one spiral belly without human anatomy.

scenes.text: You practice short movements beside the bank, keep the battles brief, and watch how it responds to your voice.
scenes.action: Nico guides Poliwag through a short practice movement along the water's edge, crouching to watch its response. New action, same bank/reeds/tree geometry, no second tadpole.

scenes.text: Charmander waits nearby, then joins in. You'd worried about replacing your starter. It seems quite happy to let someone else get wet.
scenes.action: Charmander rests on the LEFT dry bank next to Nico while Poliwag splashes in shallow water. The starter stays dry and relaxed, tail flame safely above the ground; one of each.

scenes.text: When you challenge Brock again, you begin with Poliwag. A water attack gives you an opening, but you still have to call it before Onix closes the distance.
scenes.action: Gym rematch: Poliwag sends a small water stream toward the same single Onix as Nico gives a timed command. Brock behind Onix, not beside Nico. Clear near-versus-far trainer sides.

scenes.text: You move your Pokemon back, let it settle, and try again. Charmander watches from beside your boot after its own turn in the fight.
scenes.action: Poliwag retreats to a safer position after attacking; Charmander watches beside Nico's boot, not fighting simultaneously. Single Onix across court, room and rock layout unchanged.

scenes.text: You win the Boulder Badge and turn it over in your hand while Brock talks.
scenes.action: Close exchange: Brock hands Nico ONE small grey Boulder Badge at the court edge. No full badge row, trophy, floating medal or duplicate white hands.

scenes.text: At the Center, you open the case to show Charmander. It sniffs the badge and goes back to eating. You'd imagined a more emotional response.
scenes.action: Nico presents an open small case with ONE earned grey badge and seven empty slots beside Charmander's orange food bowl on the bench-side floor. Charmander sniffs then focuses on food. No third partner added.

scenes.text: Milo is waiting near the next town with a badge of his own. You want to tell him exactly how you earned yours.
scenes.action: Quiet roadside practice court used for the meeting: Milo shows his own small grey badge while Nico gestures about his first win. No claim this is the same first-battle moment; their current case each holds one badge.

scenes.text: He wants a battle. This time, you ask for a chance to rest first, and he agrees.
scenes.action: Nico asks for time to rest, holding a calm palm-out gesture; Milo agrees, Charmander resting at Nico's near side. No battle effects, no duplicate costume on rival.

scenes.text: When you finally face each other, you use Pidgey to give Charmander a break and make Milo adjust his plan.
scenes.action: Their rested battle: Pidgey circles above Nico's side while Milo and Squirtle adjust position on the far side. Charmander is resting OFFSCREEN, do not insert a second battle starter.

scenes.text: You still lose, but you understand the loss while it's happening. You saw the change he made, just too late to answer it.
scenes.action: Milo directs Squirtle toward a new angle as Nico realizes the change too late, reaching to recall his tired Pidgey. One readable action, not several flying bird copies.

scenes.text: That evening, you write down the moment instead of blaming your Pokemon.
scenes.action: At the right log Nico writes a small note about the battle beside resting Charmander; paper has short abstract marks only, no readable caption. White face/hands stay flat bright white at night.

scenes.text: Your next badge comes from Misty in Cerulean City. Her Water-type team means Charmander spends part of the match watching you rely on someone else.
scenes.action: Misty and Psyduck on the far pool platform, Nico commands Pidgey from the left walkway. Charmander watches near Nico's boot and does not attack. Clear team ownership, no extra Pokemon or humans.

scenes.text: Pidgey has to keep moving, and you have to resist giving a new instruction every time you're nervous.
scenes.action: Closer match action: Pidgey keeps moving above the LEFT safe walkway while Psyduck sends a small water attack from the pool's far platform. Nico hesitates rather than giving conflicting commands.

scenes.text: Later, an Electric-type opponent makes that same bird a poor choice. You're beginning to prepare for the Pokemon in front of you.
scenes.action: Electric matchup example: Raichu stands across the marked floor with a small controlled yellow spark; Nico prepares to recall Pidgey before it gets caught. No human yellow-tinted skin or enormous lightning explosion.

scenes.text: Training sessions change with the next Gym, and so does the order you send your partners out. You keep the badge case closed while you're deciding.
scenes.action: Nico organizes a short practice sequence for his three small partners around camp. Closed badge case beside the folded map on the right log. Three distinct species, no imagined evolved forms.

scenes.text: After enough practice and battles, Charmander evolves into Charmeleon.
scenes.action: The result of the starter evolution: ONE red Charmeleon stands by the tent, a few fading glow particles around its body; Nico looks at the taller partner. Do not also draw Charmander or a ghost of it.

scenes.text: You wake up with a partner that takes up more of the tent entrance and can no longer fit on your lap the same way.
scenes.action: Charmeleon occupies the tent entrance while seated Nico makes room on the outside mat; its tail flame remains far from canvas. Compact Nico, creature a little taller, no change to tent architecture.

scenes.text: Its reach has changed. So has the space it needs to turn.
scenes.action: Closer full-creature profile near the green tent: Charmeleon stretches one forearm and carefully turns its longer tail in the clear space. One continuous tail, no extra horn or wing.

scenes.text: During your next practice, you give a command that worked for Charmander and watch Charmeleon overshoot the target. You spend the afternoon adjusting.
scenes.action: Practice at the pond's dry LEFT bank: Charmeleon has overshot a small flat target stone, Nico gestures to slow the next attempt. Creature stays on land with safe flame, not swimming or fighting Poliwag.

scenes.text: Evolution helps your team, but it also means learning the Pokemon you already thought you knew. Your familiar camping arrangement needs changing as well.
scenes.action: Nico moves the orange bowl and tan sleeping mat farther from the tent doorway to accommodate Charmeleon. Show the relocation in his hands, not an unexplained new tent location.

scenes.text: Pidgey eventually becomes Pidgeotto, and Poliwag becomes Poliwhirl. You make more room for them and change how they train together.
scenes.action: The newly evolved bird and frog train beside Nico: Pidgeotto perches on the right log, Poliwhirl stands on the bank-side camp ground with its two fists and NO tail. No earlier forms duplicated.

scenes.text: Poliwhirl can stay on its feet through exercises that used to tire it out.
scenes.action: Poliwhirl finishes a short controlled movement on the dry bank while Nico watches. One spiral belly and two white fists; pond and reeds unchanged, no earlier Poliwag.

scenes.text: Pidgeotto lands with enough force to knock over a food bowl if you put it too close to the perch.
scenes.action: Pidgeotto has just landed near the right log and knocked over ONE blue food bowl; a few food crumbs scatter on the ground. Nico reaches for the bowl. No duplicated bird trail or flying bowls.

scenes.text: You learn which partner needs a quiet morning after a difficult fight.
scenes.action: Nico lets tired Charmeleon rest on its moved tan mat near the tent, crouching to check it. Tail flame safely clear of fabric; no medical bandages or unspoken injury.

scenes.text: Your daily routine starts taking longer, even while battles get easier. You can't fit another training session into the day by skipping the time you spend looking after them.
scenes.action: Nico refills water/food for the three partners instead of hurrying into another exercise. Current orange/blue bowls and moved mat remain where he put them; right log and left tent stay fixed.

scenes.text: In Celadon City, you meet a trainer who offers to trade for Charmeleon. His Pokemon would give your team a different option, and you spend longer considering it than you expected.
scenes.action: At the right planter Trader presents his Eevee while making a trade offer; Nico listens with Charmeleon beside his leg. No transaction, no animal handed away yet, no duplicate starter or floating price text.

scenes.text: Charmeleon is asleep against your leg while the other trainer describes his offer. You ask a few questions, then tell him you're keeping your partner.
scenes.action: Closer exchange: Charmeleon dozes against Nico's boot; Nico gently declines with a white palm-out gesture and keeps the starter's ball. Trader accepts the refusal. No angry caricature or extra Pokemon.

scenes.text: On the way out of town, you buy supplies and reconsider your next Gym strategy with the team you have.
scenes.action: Nico leaves the blank-shuttered shop holding a small plain paper supply packet; Charmeleon walks next to him, one flame. No merchant face or lettering added, crate and planter still fixed.

scenes.text: You still want to win. You just want this particular Pokemon with you when you do.
scenes.action: Nico crouches to check his familiar partner before continuing along the street, Charmeleon looking back at him. Medium interaction, no future Charizard projected behind them.

scenes.text: That choice gets tested outside the city when you find Team Rocket bothering a young trainer. They're trying to take his Pokemon, and he has backed himself against a wall.
scenes.action: By the central-left alley wall, Rocket grunt reaches toward Jonah's active ball while Jonah protects one Eevee by his feet. Threat through posture, no weapon or violence on human bodies, no black human skin.

scenes.text: You could keep walking toward your next challenge. Charmeleon has already stopped.
scenes.action: Nico and Charmeleon stop at the street entrance when they notice the confrontation offscreen; Nico's hand lowers from his map. One pair, no victims/ghosts copied into this foreground detail.

scenes.text: You step beside the trainer and send Pidgeotto out to give him room to move.
scenes.action: Nico steps beside Jonah and Pidgeotto flies between them and the offscreen threat, opening room for Jonah and Eevee to move toward the alley exit. No Charmeleon inserted or bird clones.

scenes.text: The fight is messy, and a grunt's Pokemon keeps getting between you and the exit.
scenes.action: Koffing hovers low near the alley opening and blocks the way with a little purple gas; Rocket grunt gives a command from behind it. No duplicated smoke face, no gas turning white human face purple.

scenes.text: You direct Charmeleon toward that gap while the trainer recalls his partner. Once he can leave, you get your own team clear.
scenes.action: Charmeleon directs a modest controlled fire burst away from people to clear the gap around Koffing; Jonah retreats holding his recalled Eevee ball. Eevee is NOT also visible. Nico directs the retreat, one of each person.

scenes.text: Afterward, you need a Center and replacement supplies. Team Rocket hasn't given you a badge, and you've lost the afternoon you meant to spend practicing.
scenes.action: In the Celadon room with counter LEFT and bench RIGHT, nurse checks tired Charmeleon on a mat while Nico sets down depleted plain supplies. Do not copy the Viridian room layout or grey-tint faces.

scenes.text: The trainer you helped comes to thank you with his Pokemon beside him. Charmeleon takes an interest in the little creature, then returns to the nurse for another check.
scenes.action: Jonah thanks Nico by the right bench, Eevee beside his foot; Charmeleon sniffs the small creature before returning to care. One partner per owner, warm interaction without hair or eyebrows.

scenes.text: You miss your planned departure and send Milo a message saying you'll be late. He asks whether you need anything.
scenes.action: Nico on the right bench sends a message from one small unbranded grey communicator with blank simple screen; Charmeleon rests nearby. No Milo head on screen, thought bubble, written chat or extra phone.

scenes.text: You tell him where you are, and he turns back with food. It's the first time you're pleased to see him ahead of schedule.
scenes.action: Milo arrives beside the right bench and hands Nico a plain wrapped sandwich; tired Charmeleon stays on its mat nearby. Nico relaxes his posture. Same green rival jacket and blue main jacket.

scenes.text: Your rivalry changes after that. Milo still notices every mistake you make, but now he'll stay to explain what he saw.
scenes.action: On the low courtyard wall outside the Saffron Gym, Milo explains a stance error with one hand gesture; Nico listens beside standing Charmeleon. No angry finger-pointing or crowd.

scenes.text: You watch him battle and notice that his Wartortle sometimes responds before he finishes a command.
scenes.action: Friendly practice inside the marked court: Wartortle moves at Milo's short command, Poliwhirl across the court as a controlled practice opponent. Nico is OFFSCREEN, no rival duplicated in background.

scenes.text: You try giving Charmeleon the same freedom. During practice, you call the goal and let it choose the last few steps.
scenes.action: Nico points toward a simple target marker then lowers his hand, allowing Charmeleon to pick a route around the near corner marker. One partner moving on solid ground, no teleport copies.

scenes.text: Sometimes it gets distracted. Sometimes it finds a better angle than the one you were about to demand.
scenes.action: Charmeleon chooses a clear side angle around the near corner marker, Nico noticing the successful choice from his trainer side. New action within same court, no camera inset or fantasy room.

scenes.text: You keep working on it, especially when you're tired enough to want everything done your way.
scenes.action: Tired Nico pauses by the low wall instead of issuing another command; Charmeleon waits patiently at his side. Convey fatigue through posture and tiny mouth, not grey eye bags or eyebrows.

scenes.text: At the Saffron Gym, that preparation meets Sabrina. Her Psychic-type Pokemon disrupt the rhythm you've been using to win.
scenes.action: Gym challenge: Sabrina and Alakazam on the far trainer platform face Nico and Charmeleon on the near edge. Alakazam holds two spoons, no third hand or generic ghost face.

scenes.text: You send Charmeleon forward, lose track of the opponent's position, and issue two different commands before either helps.
scenes.action: Alakazam has shifted to the right side of the court while Charmeleon lunges toward an empty earlier position. Small motion marks only, ONE visible Alakazam, no translucent clone or psychic diagram.

scenes.text: Milo watches from the side while you recall it and reset. You lose the challenge.
scenes.action: Nico recalls his tired Charmeleon as Milo observes from the LEFT wall outside the boundary. Sabrina and Alakazam are OFFSCREEN in this angle. No simultaneous second main hero or extra trainer.

scenes.text: Outside, you ask him what you missed. He tells you that once you started worrying about the badge, you stopped noticing what your Pokemon was doing.
scenes.action: Outside at the low wall Nico asks Milo what he missed; Milo points back toward the Gym doorway. Map/case closed, no Charmeleon added from references to an absent-cast shot.

scenes.text: You spend the next session practicing an escape and a recall instead of another attack.
scenes.action: Controlled retry practice in the empty court: Nico raises the active recall ball while Charmeleon turns away from the target instead of attacking. No opponent or attack effect, one starter.

scenes.text: The rematch takes longer. You wait for openings you rushed past before and switch partners while they can still contribute later.
scenes.action: Rematch: Nico waits for an opening, Poliwhirl on his near side responding while Alakazam is on Sabrina's far side. Clear owner sides, no ghost clones or duplicate white fists on humans.

scenes.text: When you finally earn the badge, Charmeleon needs a rest and you let it have one. You don't leave town straight away to preserve a lead over Milo.
scenes.action: After earning the badge, Nico lets Charmeleon rest beside the low wall while Milo waits nearby; closed case at Nico's hip/hand, no full eight-badge case yet. Calm medium view.

scenes.text: During that break, it climbs onto a low wall beside you and places a paw on your sleeve, the way Charmander did after the first trip to the Center.
scenes.action: Charmeleon stands on the low wall and touches Nico's blue sleeve with one paw. Nico's round white face turns toward it; same sleeve motif, no flashback overlay or younger Charmander added.

scenes.text: You're glad you kept it. You're also glad you've finally learned to stop moving sometimes.
scenes.action: Nico sits beside resting Charmeleon on the low wall and takes an unhurried break, white mitten near its shoulder, tail flame safely to the outer side. New relaxed gesture, not a heroic victory poster.

scenes.text: Charmeleon eventually evolves into Charizard, and your carefully chosen campsite becomes too small again.
scenes.action: One newly evolved Charizard unfolds its two wings beside the small LEFT tent, Nico looking up. A few fading evolution particles; NO Charmander, Charmeleon, inset or ghost behind it.

scenes.text: You have a huge orange partner with wings and a tail you need to keep clear of the tent.
scenes.action: Nico gestures to keep Charizard's large wing and tail clear of the green canvas tent while moving its sleeping mat into open ground. Creature taller than Nico, human proportions unchanged.

scenes.text: It tests a wingbeat and sends your map into the bushes. You retrieve it while Pidgeotto watches from a branch.
scenes.action: A wingbeat has blown the cream map into the rear-left low shrubs; Nico reaches to retrieve it. Pidgeotto watches from the right-side branch, Charizard wings settling. No floating tent or second map.

scenes.text: Charizard can do things Charmander couldn't have attempted. You also have new problems to plan around.
scenes.action: Charizard makes a controlled short lift above the clearing, Nico stays safely on the ground watching. Keep one continuous tail and TWO wings, no rider or flying Nico.

scenes.text: A Flying type has weaknesses you need to respect, and the opponent who looks easy from a distance may have exactly the move you're hoping they don't.
scenes.action: A matchup lesson in the Electric training hall: Raichu has a small yellow spark ready while Nico recalls Flying-type Charizard before an unnecessary hit. No claimed new badge or stadium scoreboard.

scenes.text: At the remaining Gyms, you stop treating Charizard as the answer to every match.
scenes.action: At the near edge of the Ground Gym Nico calls Charizard back instead of sending it toward the far court; show the active recall ball, one partner still visible during recall, no double form.

scenes.text: You use Poliwhirl where water gives your team an opening and bring Pidgeotto into fights where it can work safely.
scenes.action: Poliwhirl sends a controlled water stream toward one grey Rhyhorn across the sandy field while Nico directs it. No Onix substituted for Giovanni's canonical Ground creature, no offscreen bird drawn.

scenes.text: Your partners get their turns, and Charizard gets called back when continuing would waste it.
scenes.action: Pidgeotto returns to Nico after its own safe turn, Nico preparing the active recall ball without an attack continuing. Show partner rotation through one real action, no full-team collage.

scenes.text: Pidgeotto becomes Pidgeot before your final badge challenge.
scenes.action: One newly evolved Pidgeot stands proudly beside Nico near the quiet court boundary. Long red/yellow crest and broad wings match the evolved identity, NO earlier Pidgeotto beside it.

scenes.text: By the time you defeat Giovanni at the Viridian Gym, the case has all eight badges.
scenes.action: Giovanni concedes the final Gym challenge and hands Nico the final small green geometric badge. Nico's compact white-headed adult design unchanged; no victory text or giant glowing badge.

scenes.text: You open it on the pavement outside, close it, and check whether your team has eaten. The League will still be there after dinner.
scenes.action: On the pavement outside this Ground Gym Nico checks his small open case containing EIGHT filled simple slots, then attends to his waiting team with food. One Charizard, bird and frog; no second starter.

scenes.text: The approach to the Indigo Plateau makes you understand why those badges are required. On Victory Road, trainers who've completed their own journeys can punish a poor choice as quickly as a Gym Leader.
scenes.action: Advanced practice encounter along the cave passage: Nico and Pidgeot on the near safe path face Trader and his Machamp across the wider bend. Machamp correctly has FOUR creature arms; humans have TWO each.

scenes.text: You arrive at the League tired, with notes full of corrections.
scenes.action: Nico arrives tired at the League foyer carrying one small notebook with abstract correction marks, closed badge case in the other hand. Blue bench left and recovery stand right, no Pokemon or crowd.

scenes.text: Inside, you look at the doors leading toward the Elite Four and feel the urge to start immediately. Your partners have been traveling all day.
scenes.action: Nico hesitates before the rear double doors with his tired team gathered near him. Charizard wings folded to fit the hall; Pidgeot and Poliwhirl grounded, no giant human body.

scenes.text: You arrange a rest, check your supplies, and ask Milo when he plans to challenge. He has already been turned away by a loss and is preparing to try again.
scenes.action: Nico and Milo talk on the left bench while checking supplies on a small plain packet between them. Keep rival outfit green and main outfit blue, no full team or extra trainers inserted.

scenes.text: Your first League run ends against Lorelei. You recognize Ice-type Pokemon and assume Charizard should handle the fight.
scenes.action: First League attempt: Lorelei and Lapras on the far shallow pool side face Nico and Charizard on the near dry platform. All humans flat white, ice-blue court geometry preserved.

scenes.text: Then one of her partners uses a Water-type attack, and you realize how little your first glance told you.
scenes.action: Lapras sends a modest Water attack across the pool toward Charizard; Nico reacts with a recall gesture. No ice-only attack, massive flood or tinted human skin.

scenes.text: You bring Poliwhirl in without a clear follow-up and lose the opening you needed.
scenes.action: Poliwhirl takes the near position but hesitates as Nico looks unsure about the follow-up; Lapras ready across water. Charizard has been recalled and is NOT also visible.

scenes.text: Before long, you're outside with your team recalled and your eight badges still in their case. Nobody takes them away. They just haven't made you ready for this room.
scenes.action: Nico sits outside the rear doors on the steps, all partners recalled, holding a small OPEN case with EIGHT earned badges. No missing badges or Pokemon appearing through closed balls.

scenes.text: You sit on the steps until you can discuss the match without making excuses.
scenes.action: Closer pose on the same steps: Nico closes the badge case and reviews his notes, accepting the lost challenge. Plain papers, black dot eyes and tiny mouth, no written inspirational caption.

scenes.text: Milo meets you there with Blastoise beside him. He doesn't look surprised.
scenes.action: Milo comes to the steps with one Blastoise beside him and sits near Nico. Both grey cannons are attached to the turtle shell. No Squirtle/Wartortle or ghost history image.

scenes.text: You tell him you kept choosing moves to rescue the previous mistake, and he nods because he's done it too.
scenes.action: Nico explains his choices to Milo with a small open-hand gesture; Milo listens and nods. Partners OFFSCREEN, focus on their exchange without imagined battle screens.

scenes.text: You watch a practice battle together and start writing down possibilities before deciding on an attack.
scenes.action: Friendly League practice: Nico watches Pidgeot's movement while Milo works with Blastoise across the court; both trainers study rather than rush the next command. One bird, one turtle.

scenes.text: You also stop training when your partners get tired, even if you haven't finished what you planned. Charizard settles near you while you work.
scenes.action: Nico stops practice and writes notes on the left bench while Charizard settles beside it with wings folded. Blank-marked notebook, tail held safely in open floor space, no duplicate creature.

scenes.text: The Champion is close enough to tempt you into hurrying, but you stay outside the League until you can explain how your whole team will get through it.
scenes.action: Nico reviews the next route with his three rested partners, looking at each before approaching the double doors. One of each teammate, one trainer, no aura or badge ranking diagram.

scenes.text: On your next attempt, you handle Lorelei with the matchups you actually face.
scenes.action: Second Lorelei challenge: Nico calmly directs Poliwhirl from near dry platform while Lapras waits on the far pool side. Actual clear matchup, no former Charizard pasted in to show failure.

scenes.text: Against Bruno, you keep Pidgeot available for his Fighting-type Pokemon and let Poliwhirl handle the opponents it can counter.
scenes.action: Bruno's arena: Pidgeot uses space above the near tan court while Machamp prepares across from it; Nico and covered brown-gi Bruno stand on their separate trainer sides. Four creature arms only.

scenes.text: Agatha makes you work through a battle where attacking too quickly can waste a turn.
scenes.action: Agatha challenge: Nico pauses before a command as one Gengar lurks on the far purple court and Charizard waits near him. Agatha holds her cane at the far side. No ghost Nico, transparent overlays or extra Gengar.

scenes.text: Each victory leaves you with another decision about recovery and which partner needs help first. You check them between rooms.
scenes.action: Between rooms Nico checks the team beside the RIGHT recovery stand, holding one plain Potion bottle and tending the most tired partner. Same foyer layout, no three nurses or restoration text.

scenes.text: You reach Lance with enough left to continue, and he sends out a Pokemon you've been worried about since you started studying the League.
scenes.action: Nico enters Lance's emerald-trimmed arena, one Dragonite taking the far battle position while red-caped Lance gives the opening command. No Charizard for this revealing opponent frame.

scenes.text: His Dragonite forces you to use a plan that takes your whole team.
scenes.action: Nico studies Dragonite across the court and readies Poliwhirl on his near side. Dragonite has two antennae, small teal wings and NO flaming tail, distinct from the main Charizard.

scenes.text: Poliwhirl contributes the Ice Beam you've been practicing, but you have to keep it ready long enough to use it.
scenes.action: Poliwhirl sends ONE pale-blue Ice Beam toward the far Dragonite at Nico's timed command. Frog has no tail, human has only two arms, no literal ice cage around Nico.

scenes.text: Pidgeot gives you another option when staying in would be costly.
scenes.action: Nico switches to Pidgeot to give his other partner time, Pidgeot moving clear of Dragonite's line across the emerald court. No Poliwhirl still fighting simultaneously.

scenes.text: Charizard finishes a part of the battle without being asked to carry all of it.
scenes.action: Charizard enters for its assigned part of the fight, wings held clear of Nico, controlled fire aimed across toward Dragonite. One dragon-like creature of each species, no duplicate main starter.

scenes.text: You win and check your partners while the result settles in.
scenes.action: The battle has ended; Nico checks his three partners at the near boundary while Lance acknowledges them from his far position. No trophy or Champion celebration yet.

scenes.text: There's still a Champion through the next doorway. For a moment, you wish the League finished here. Then you hear a voice you recognize from Pallet Town.
scenes.action: Nico pauses before a different opened rear door and looks toward the voice calling from beyond. Keep him SINGLE, no visible imagined Milo, no role ladder or red throne.

scenes.text: Milo made it through before you. Blastoise is standing beside him, and your friend is wearing the expression he had when Squirtle inspected his shoe at Oak's lab.
scenes.action: Champion reveal: green-jacket Milo stands at the far red trainer stand with his one Blastoise, Nico at the near blue side. No Squirtle memory inset or second Milo face in background.

scenes.text: He congratulates you for reaching him. You look at the team he has ready and understand why he won.
scenes.action: Milo congratulates Nico with a friendly gesture from across the quiet court; Nico looks at the ready opponent. The turtle remains beside Milo, no added unreferenced team members.

scenes.text: You also know what he expects you to do. He's watched you rely on Charizard when a match becomes difficult.
scenes.action: Closer two-trainer faceoff from the SAME court: Nico considers the opening with active ball in white mitten; Milo waits on his far stand. Pokemon OFFSCREEN in this shot, no future-power ghost.

scenes.text: You send Pidgeot out first. Milo pauses, calls his own opening, and starts the battle you've both been working toward since the day you left home.
scenes.action: Nico opens with Pidgeot on the near court, Milo reacts then directs Blastoise from the far side. Charizard NOT visible or depicted on an inset, clear ownership and one of each.

scenes.text: He makes you use the habits he helped you build. You recognize a move he's preparing and switch before it catches the wrong partner.
scenes.action: Nico recognizes Blastoise's prepared water move and recalls Pidgeot before the stream reaches its old position. One bird still visible during recall, no second bird inside ball.

scenes.text: He answers by changing his plan. Poliwhirl earns an opening, and you bring it back while it can still help.
scenes.action: Poliwhirl creates a small opening with a quick movement, Nico prepares to recall it while still able to help. Blastoise adjusting opposite; no fainted second frog or electric attack invented.

scenes.text: When Charizard finally enters, Blastoise is waiting. You remember standing with Charmander while Squirtle stayed beyond its reach.
scenes.action: Final partners face each other: Charizard near Nico, Blastoise near Milo. Reference the first fight through comparable spacing only, no ghost Charmander/Squirtle or duplicate trainer.

scenes.text: This time, you check your partner before giving the command. Charizard has room to move and enough strength left.
scenes.action: Nico checks Charizard's posture before giving a short command, Charizard steady with wings half-folded; Blastoise waits farther away. His pure-white head never gets red flame reflections.

scenes.text: You wait for Milo's attack, call the response you've practiced, and watch your partner take it.
scenes.action: Blastoise's controlled water stream arrives; Charizard moves clear and responds at Nico's practiced timing. One coherent readable action, no explosive fire-water collage or flying main trainer.

scenes.text: The referee calls the result. Milo returns Blastoise, walks across the field, and offers his hand. You've become the Kanto Champion.
scenes.action: Milo has recalled Blastoise and crossed the court to offer Nico his white mitten hand. Nico accepts beside the center boundary. No visible referee, winner text, trophy or duplicated Champion.

scenes.text: You're trying to answer him when Charizard presses its head against your shoulder, nearly knocking you over.
scenes.action: Charizard lowers its large orange head against Nico's shoulder in affection, Nico leaning to keep his balance. Tail flame behind and clear, one large partner, one compact adult trainer.

scenes.text: Pidgeot lands nearby and Poliwhirl steps up beside it.
scenes.action: The three winning partners gather around Nico, Pidgeot landing on the ground and Poliwhirl stepping beside it. Distinct species and one of each, no full-body duplicate pose lineup.

scenes.text: Later, Oak records your team in the Hall of Fame. You keep looking at the Pokemon beside you while he works.
scenes.action: Oak at the left desk records the three partners while Nico stands with them beside the low central podium. Unmarked display, no extra Pokemon silhouettes, no text captions.

scenes.text: They're hungry, and you're going to have to find somewhere with enough space for Charizard before anyone gets dinner.
scenes.action: Nico notices hungry partners, holding one plain food packet as Charizard folds its wings to fit; the bird and frog look toward him. Ordinary need after the win, no victory poster.

scenes.text: On your return to Viridian City, you stop at the Center that treated Charmander after your first battle.
scenes.action: Return to the ORIGINAL Viridian Center facade: Nico approaches with his grown team; Charizard larger than doorway but wings folded, same central awning/windows/steps/hedge/lamp. No city replacement.

scenes.text: The nurse comes out to meet your team. Charizard has to lower its head to see her through the doorway.
scenes.action: Nurse stands at the original doorway and Charizard lowers its head so she can see it; Nico thanks her beside his partner. One nurse, one trainer, one evolved starter, no younger Charmander inset.

scenes.text: You thank her, then notice a new trainer on the waiting bench with a frightened partner and a map spread across his knees.
scenes.action: Nico notices a different maroon-hoodie beginner on the LEFT blue bench, cream route map on knees, frightened Eevee at his feet. The RIGHT mint counter and central doorway remain the original room.

scenes.text: You sit beside him and ask what happened. Charizard settles outside the window, keeping its tail clear of the wall.
scenes.action: Charizard rests OUTSIDE by the original LEFT window, tail flame held clear of cream wall, wings folded and peaceful. No human-sized dragon, duplicate head or nurse drawn from references.

scenes.text: You listen while the trainer explains the command he wishes he hadn't given.
scenes.action: Nico sits beside the beginner on the original LEFT bench, leans to listen with a gentle white-mitten gesture. Map stays on beginner's knees, Eevee close to his shoe. End on this concrete interaction, no text.
